items.question: Will the core reach an IETF working group?
items.context: The draft is an individual submission. It moved to a new name (draft-httpauth-payment-00 on 2026-06-19, -01 on 2026-09-09) while the old name was still active, and the old name expired on 2026-09-18. mpp.dev's standards-track wording is stronger than the Datatracker record. On 2026-11-11 the maintainers edited -01 in place rather than posting -02, so the IETF copy now lags paymentauth.org, and an open pull request (2026-11-13) would make in-place edits the rule. At IETF 127 on 2026-11-20 the HTTP working group heard draft-nottingham-httpbis-402-00, a separate individual draft that would define only the meaning of 402, with no registries or headers. Its slides list draft-httpauth-payment among current uses of the code, and a show of hands on interest in adopting it gave 15 yes, 3 no and 18 no opinion. The MPP draft itself had no new revision and no Datatracker event since 2026-09-09.

items.question: Will session become a standardized intent?
items.context: The contribution rules need two methods, and as of 2026-10-21 six methods define session, yet PR #280 closed unmerged on 2026-09-28. A second attempt, PR #387, closed unmerged on 2026-11-07; its successor, PR #394, was still open on 2026-11-21, so session stays per method until a merge.

items.question: How much MPP activity is real commerce?
items.context: On 2026-10-21 MPPscan's last 30 days averaged about one cent (1.1 cents) per transaction (785,833 transactions, 8,620 USD). Read on 2026-11-14, its indexed data stopped at 2026-11-11; per indexed day it showed about 20,100 transactions and 327 USD (about 1.6 cents each), against about 26,200 and 287 USD on 2026-10-21. The missing days are an indexing gap, not evidence of a fall in use. Read again on 2026-11-21, the all-time totals were unchanged and the 7-day window read zero, so the indexer was still stalled; the 30-day window then held only about 20 indexed days. On 2026-11-21, 139 of 142 directory listings accepted Tempo. MPPscan publishes no counting method, while Visa and Artemis exclude identified wash and test activity from their totals.

items.question: Does Stripe's published 1.5 percent stablecoin fee apply to MPP charges?
items.context: Stripe's US pricing page lists stablecoin payments at 1.5 percent of the amount, with gas sponsorship included, and Shared Payment Tokens at 0.15 USD per SPT issued. The MPP docs list only minimums and do not say which rates apply to MPP charges.

items.question: Should channels expire?
items.context: Tempo, EVM and Hedera channels and vouchers have no expiry, and the Tempo spec only advises servers to close channels idle for about 30 days. Solana vouchers can carry expiresAt and XRPL channels Expiration or CancelAfter.

items.question: Will MPP gain a user authorization object, or rely on AP2-style mandates?
items.context: The MPP core defines no user mandate. Method-level grants (Tempo access keys, SPT usage limits, debit mandates for subscriptions) authorize payments but do not record what the user asked an agent to buy. As of 2026-10-21 neither the MPP specs nor the AP2 repository refers to the other.

items.question: Will Mastercard publish an MPP method or statement of its own?
items.context: Only Tempo's quote inside Mastercard's 2026-06-10 release exists, and no method spec; Mastercard's 2026-10-20 Early Access brief builds Agent Pay for Machines on x402 and names no MPP.

items.question: Have the 12 MPP findings in arXiv:2609.00060 been fixed in the specs or SDKs?
items.context: Table III counts 12 new and 9 known MPP cases, such as MPP-14, where a retry after a lost response counts Tempo session spend twice. The authors say they reported the new cases and that the counts are not demonstrated production vulnerabilities. mppx 0.14.0 (2026-10-21) added idempotency keys for Tempo session charges; no source links it to MPP-14.

items.question: Will MPP's MCP binding move off error codes that MCP reserves?
items.context: draft-payment-transport-mcp-00 requires -32042 and -32043, but -32042 means URL elicitation required in MCP 2025-11-25, and MCP 2026-07-28 reserves -32020 to -32099 for its own codes. Issue #374 has been open since 2026-10-05. PR #392, which proposed a tool-result signal for tools/call and -31042 and -31043 for other requests, was closed unmerged by its author on 2026-11-17, and mppx and mpp-go still use -32042.
